import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a FacetGrid to plot survival rates across different categories
# This visualization shows the interaction between passenger class, sex, and where they embarked.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x="pclass",
    y="survived",
    hue="sex",
    col="embark_town",
    kind="bar",
    height=5,
    aspect=0.8,
    palette={"male": "#5499c7", "female": "#f1948a"},
    legend=False # We will create a custom legend
)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---

# Set overall title
g.fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Rate by Class, Sex, and Embarkation Port', fontsize=16, y=1.03)

# Customize axis labels and titles
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")
g.set_titles("Embarked: {col_name}")

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
    ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='-', alpha=0.8)

    # Add data labels on top of each bar
    for p in ax.patches:
        ax.annotate(
            f'{p.get_height():.0%}',
            (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
            ha='center',
            va='center',
            xytext=(0, 9),
            textcoords='offset points',
            fontsize=9,
            color='black'
        )

# Adjust the layout to make room for the suptitle and legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# Add a custom legend
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', labels=['Male', 'Female'])


# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
